BackgroundNoise.description:
The background noise, one level for the experiment: looped on every speaker unequalised, faded in over 2 s once
the task file is read at Go (OpenRigs.Audio SpeakerMixer).

levelDbfs.description: The background noise's level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its whole length as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3). The lab's default -50. The workflow stops as the sound's buffer is built (at Go for a sound built once, at its trial for one built each trial) if any peak would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix
levelDbfs.title: LevelDbfs

BackgroundNoise.title: BackgroundNoise

OptogeneticsSettings.description:
Zapit optogenetic stimulation: the lab's block (open_rigs.core.task Optogenetics) and this task's laser timing.

The stimulation sites and ramp-down are set in the Zapit conditions file loaded in Zapit, not here; Bonsai reads
the same file to list its conditions. "Stimulus" is the tone and grating; the laser is continuous: it starts at the
trigger (the trigger line's rising edge on a hardware-triggered rig), laser_to_stimulus_seconds before the first
tone pip (after it if negative), in whole 50 ms steps and at most 0.2 s, and Bonsai stops it at the trial's
outcome, or after laser_max_seconds if that comes first. A trial that ends before its trigger has no laser.

enabled.description: Whether this is an optogenetics experiment, Zapit running it: every trial sends it a condition from the conditions file (laser off at 0 mW on laser-off trials: the galvos move and the masking light shows), and the launching app checks Zapit is answering before Go
enabled.title: Enabled

zapitConditionsPath.description: Path to the Zapit conditions file loaded in Zapit. Its top-level stimLocations01, stimLocations02, ... entries are the conditions, numbered 1 to N with no gaps. The launching app keeps a copy beside the task file at Go
zapitConditionsPath.title: ZapitConditionsPath

laserPowerMw.description: Laser power on laser-on trials, in mW, the same for every condition: sent to Zapit with each StartStimulus (overriding the conditions file's power; Zapit's laser calibration turns it into volts) and logged as laserPowerMw (0 on laser-off trials). Required with optogenetics on
laserPowerMw.title: LaserPowerMw

laserOnProbability.description: Probability that a trial after trialsBeforeLaser is a laser-on trial, shared equally by every condition in the conditions file; all other trials are laser-off trials, sent a condition with the laser off
laserOnProbability.title: LaserOnProbability

laserToStimulusSeconds.description: Signed, in seconds: the trigger (the ZapitTrigger line) comes this long before the stimulus; 0 with it; negative after it. The trial's start is the end of the interval less the lead, max(this, 0), once the quiet waits hold, and the stimulus comes the lead after the trial's start in every experiment, optogenetics on or off, so timing never reveals Zapit; the trigger only with optogenetics. Zapit is armed during the interval and adds no time. Refused above itiMinSeconds - 0.2 s (Zapit's reply margin); each task adds its own limits
laserToStimulusSeconds.title: LaserToStimulusSeconds

trialsBeforeLaser.description: Trials at the experiment's start with no laser-on trial among them (each still sends Zapit a condition, at 0 mW); laserOnProbability applies from the next trial
trialsBeforeLaser.title: TrialsBeforeLaser

laserMaxSeconds.description: Longest the laser stays on in one trial, in seconds from the trigger, timed by Bonsai; it then ramps down over the condition's offRampDownDuration_ms. A safety cap: the laser normally stops at the trial's outcome. Timed on the Harp clock, with a wall-clock backstop should the board stall. With optogenetics on it must be at least the longest stage responseWindowSeconds + laser_to_stimulus_seconds + 0.25 s (the laser runs from the first pip less laser_to_stimulus_seconds to at most the first pip plus responseWindowSeconds), so it never ends the laser before the response window closes; on a stage without responseWindowSeconds a longer trial loses its laser before the outcome
laserMaxSeconds.title: LaserMaxSeconds

triggerHoldSeconds.description: How long the trigger line, and the masking light on it, stays high after the outcome, in seconds, on every trial of an optogenetics experiment (the line stays low without optogenetics): at least 0.5, the longest ramp-down a conditions file may have, and at most trialStructure.itiMinSeconds - laser_to_stimulus_seconds - 0.2 s, since the next trial is armed once the line falls and Zapit's reply needs 0.2 s before its trigger
triggerHoldSeconds.title: TriggerHoldSeconds

penaltyTimeoutSeconds). Each task says which trials are penalised; timeoutSeconds has no lab default: each task file gives it.

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout after a penalised trial, in seconds; the next interval starts after it
timeoutSeconds.title: TimeoutSeconds

sound.description: The penalty sound, with every timeout

levelDbfs.description: The penalty sound's level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its whole length as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3). The lab's default -30. The workflow stops as the sound's buffer is built (at Go for a sound built once, at its trial for one built each trial) if any peak would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix

RewardTone.description: A task's reward tone, played at levelDbfs.

levelDbfs.description: The reward tone's level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its whole length as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3). The lab's default -36. The workflow stops as the sound's buffer is built (at Go for a sound built once, at its trial for one built each trial) if any peak would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix
levelDbfs.title: LevelDbfs

StimulusOff.description:
Where the stimulus switches off on a stimulus-off trial (a stage's stimulusOffProbability says how often).

On a stimulus-off trial each listed stimulus switches off once the mouse has run a track fraction of the trial's
track (position / trackLengthCm); an unlisted stimulus stays on. Everything else about the trial is unchanged, so
it is still rewarded as normal: the animal has to keep going and find the reward zone without the stimulus.

trackFractions.description: Where the stimulus switches off, as a fraction of the trial's track length, split evenly over stimulus-off trials
trackFractions.title: TrackFractions

stimuli.description: The stimuli that switch off on a stimulus-off trial: auditory (the tone), visual (the grating) or both
stimuli.title: Stimuli

StimulusOff.title: StimulusOff

StimulusSound.description: A task's stimulus sounds, each played at levelDbfs (OpenRigs.Audio SpeakerBuffer or SpeakerSet.Buffer).

levelDbfs.description: Each stimulus sound's level in dBFS RMS: the RMS of the sound over its whole length as the task gives it, before the speaker's equalisation, against full scale (a full-scale sine is -3). The lab's default -30. The workflow stops as the sound's buffer is built (at Go for a sound built once, at its trial for one built each trial) if any peak would reach -1 dBFS after equalisation. Sounds overlapping on a speaker share its headroom: each buffer's peak is checked, not their mix
levelDbfs.title: LevelDbfs

id.title: Id

label.description: The stage's label in the pipeline
label.title: Label

sha256.description: The sha256 of the pipeline file's text rig-control ran it from

TrainingPipeline.title: TrainingPipeline

TrialCondition.description:
One kind of trial in the mix: its label, its relative weight, its condition-level values (set) by dotted path and its
pairs, coen-dome-decision-making's shape. The corridor has no condition fields yet (x-conditionFields is empty), so set and
pairs are empty, and the label (one of TRIAL_TYPES) is what the corridor shows.

label.description: What the trial shows, logged as trialType: visual (the grating alone), auditory (the tone sweep alone) or audiovisualCoherent (both); here it drives the draw, as no condition field does yet
label.title: Label

weight.description: Relative draw weight: each new trial picks a condition with these as relative chances
weight.title: Weight

pairs.description: Groups of x-conditionFields paths whose lists share one pick per trial; none in this task yet
pairs.title: Pairs

set.description: Condition-level values by dotted path (x-conditionFields); none in this task yet
set.title: Set

TrialCondition.title: TrialCondition

TrialStructure.description: Timing of each trial. The inter-trial interval (open_rigs.core.task Iti) runs from the last trial's outcome (after any penalty timeout; trial 1: the first clock tick after Go) to this trial's first tone pip, with a quiet mouse. It includes the time to drink a reward (Tom Childs' fixed 2 s before his 0 or 1 s). The wheel quiet wait (open_rigs.core.task WheelQuietWait) is here, the same for every stage; the lick quiet wait is each stage's.

wheelQuietSeconds.description: Quiet wait: a trial's start needs this long with the wheel still, in seconds, counted from the interval's start: the wheel's distance (forward and back added) over the last wheelQuietSeconds must stay within wheelQuietCm; 0: off (with wheelQuietCm 0); at most 10 s
wheelQuietSeconds.title: WheelQuietSeconds

wheelQuietCm.description: The most the wheel may move, forward and back added, within the last wheelQuietSeconds before the trial's start, in cm; 0: off (with wheelQuietSeconds 0); at most 20 cm
wheelQuietCm.title: WheelQuietCm

itiMinSeconds.description: Lower bound of the inter-trial interval, drawn uniformly for every trial, in seconds; the quiet waits can only lengthen it (quietWaitSeconds)
itiMinSeconds.title: ItiMinSeconds

itiMaxSeconds.description: Upper bound of the inter-trial interval, in seconds; at least itiMinSeconds
itiMaxSeconds.title: ItiMaxSeconds

trackLengthsCm.description: Track lengths, one drawn per trial, in track cm (the mouse runs track cm / the stage's wheelGain of wheel)
trackLengthsCm.title: TrackLengthsCm

TrialStructure.title: TrialStructure

UclOpenCoenDomeNavigationTaskParameters.description:
Task parameters for the coen-dome-navigation corridor: the reward, the trial mix, the sounds, the trial structure, the penalty, stimulus off, optogenetics and what a training stage sets (the flat values below, stage 0's by default; the lick quiet wait, response window and auto-reward are the lab's, open_rigs.core.task).

A lick first counts from the trial's first tone pip, where the response window starts. Auto-reward is given on the pip whose tone reaches the reward zone's floor, no lick needed, and the trial's licks are ignored (outcomeReason FrequencyReached); on the other trials only a lick in the zone is rewarded. A trial that runs out of time or track with the tone in the zone, or ends outside the zone, is penalised. The reward is given on the left spout's valve, planned from the valve's calibration (calibration\RewardValve-Left.json); an uncalibrated valve stops the workflow at Start.

autoRewardProbability.description: Probability that a trial is an auto-reward trial, rewarded on reaching the zone's floor without a lick; 0: never, 1: every trial
autoRewardProbability.title: AutoRewardProbability

responseWindowSeconds.description: The response window, in seconds from when a lick first counts (the task says when); with no response by its end the trial is NoResponse. Null or left out: no limit (a task may refuse it)
responseWindowSeconds.title: ResponseWindowSeconds

lickQuietSeconds.description: Quiet wait: a trial's start needs this long with every spout released, in seconds, counted from the interval's start and restarted by every touch and release; a held contact (a paw or chin on a spout) holds the trial's start until released, so licks for the last reward cannot carry into the next trial; 0: off; at most 10 s. It lengthens the interval only when the mouse licks late in it (quietWaitSeconds)
lickQuietSeconds.title: LickQuietSeconds

rngSeed.description: Seed of the random number generator for these task parameters
rngSeed.title: RngSeed

trialConditions.description: The trial mix: each new trial picks one condition at random with the weights as relative chances, independently of every other trial, and shows its label (visual, auditory or audiovisualCoherent; trialType in the trial row). One whole value: a pipeline stage's conditions replace it; the trialCondition column is its 0-based index
trialConditions.title: TrialConditions

auditoryStimulus.description: The tone sweep's pips (src/sounds/all_waveforms.bin), each played at levelDbfs (open_rigs.core.task StimulusSound)
auditoryStimulus.title: AuditoryStimulus

rewardTone.description: The reward tone (src/sounds/reward_tone.bin), played at levelDbfs (open_rigs.core.task RewardTone)

backgroundNoise.description: The lab's background white noise (rig.yml's speakerArray.backgroundNoise) on every speaker, from Ready at the level of the task file as launched (open_rigs.core.task BackgroundNoise)

visualStimulus.description: The grating's spatial frequencies along the track

penalty.description: The timeout and penalty sound a penalised trial gets (open_rigs.core.task Penalty)

stimulusOff.description: Where and which stimuli switch off on a stimulus-off trial

rewardFloorHz.description: Lower frequency of the reward zone, in Hz, above the sweep's start (src/sounds/sweep.json)
rewardFloorHz.title: RewardFloorHz

rewardCeilingHz.description: Upper frequency of the reward zone, in Hz, at most the sweep's end (src/sounds/sweep.json)
rewardCeilingHz.title: RewardCeilingHz

wrongLickLimit.description: Licks outside the zone that end the trial; 0: wrong licks never end it
wrongLickLimit.title: WrongLickLimit

wheelGain.description: Track cm per wheel cm: the track's tone and grating move this many cm for each cm the wheel turns, so the mouse runs track length / wheelGain cm of wheel to the end
wheelGain.title: WheelGain

autoProgressPerSecond.description: Fraction of the track the tone and grating advance per second on their own from the trial start, added to what the wheel sets; 0: none. Moves the stimulus only: the track's end and the stimulus-off points are judged on the wheel alone
autoProgressPerSecond.title: AutoProgressPerSecond

stimulusOffProbability.description: Probability that a trial is a stimulus-off trial (stimulusOff): its listed stimuli switch off part way along the track; 0: never, 1: every trial
stimulusOffProbability.title: StimulusOffProbability

trainingPipeline.description: The training pipeline stage these values came from (id, label, sha256 of the pipeline file), filled by rig-control at launch; Go refuses a task whose id is missing or differs from the TrainingStage setting
trainingPipeline.title: TrainingPipeline

spatialFrequencyStartCpd.description: The grating's spatial frequency at the track's start, in cycles per degree
spatialFrequencyStartCpd.title: SpatialFrequencyStartCpd

spatialFrequencyEndCpd.description: The grating's spatial frequency at the track's end, in cycles per degree
